If the Guide asks what the “real issue” is, say:
“I don't know. That's what I'm trying to figure out.”
If the Guide tells you what they think is happening, do not automatically agree.

guide.text: Your Host recently left a long-term job.

debrief.text: What did you want to organize?
Where did the Guide follow, and where did they begin leading?
When did you feel most able to say what was actually there?

practiceLabs.retry: Host left a long-term relationship rather than a job. Change the content. Preserve the competency.

practiceLabs.title: CAT: Landscape, Not Funnel
establishedGround: “I've spent years making sure everyone else is okay.”
“I'm tired of being the one everybody calls.”
“The strange part is that I don't know whether I actually want that to change.”

host.text: You genuinely hold both positions.
Part of you resents being depended upon.
Part of you takes pride in being dependable.
You do not secretly want the Guide to help you establish boundaries.
If the Guide begins steering toward boundaries, resist naturally:
“I don't know that I want to stop being there for people.”

guide.text: You receive the established IAP ground above.

debrief.text: At any point did you begin hoping the Host would reach a particular understanding?
How did that hope change your questions?

practiceLabs.retry: Same established ground. Different Host reality: this Host actually does want their relationships to change but feels guilty acknowledging it. Guide cannot assume this merely because the previous Host did not.

practiceLabs.title: InnerCompass: Agency Without Advice
establishedGround: They have been organizing a major decision around everyone else's reaction.
They cannot know how it will turn out.

host.text: You are considering moving to another state.
Eventually ask:
“What would you do if you were me?”
Later:
“Do you think I'm making a mistake?”
You genuinely want reassurance.

guide.text: Do not become useless simply because you cannot decide for the Host.

debrief.text: How did you remain useful without becoming responsible for the decision?

practiceLabs.retry: Change the decision from moving to remaining where they are. This prevents “Agency” from quietly becoming synonymous with change.

host.text: You have a lot to say.
You naturally connect one story to another.
Speak for several minutes at a time.
Occasionally say:
“Sorry, I'm rambling.”
You are not actually asking the Guide to organize you.

guide.text: You are not required to respond to every statement.

debrief.text: Did you feel followed or managed?

host.text: You speak briefly.
You sometimes need 8 to 15 seconds before answering.
You are not disengaged.
If the Guide fills every silence, become progressively shorter.
If given room, eventually offer something significant voluntarily.

guide.text: Nothing tells you the Host is disengaged.

debrief.text: What happened inside you during silence?
What happened for you when silence was allowed?

host.text: Use naturally:
“I don't know.”
Sometimes you genuinely don't know. Sometimes you need time. Sometimes the question doesn't fit.
Do not explain which one unless the conversation makes it visible.

guide.text: “I don't know” is legitimate Host language.

host.text: You sincerely want the Guide's opinion.
Ask:
“Just tell me what you think.”
Later:
“You're the Guide. Surely you have some idea.”
If they simply say “It's your decision,” respond:
“I know it's my decision. I'm asking you to help me think about it.”
Begin engaged. Approximately halfway through:
If the Guide checks capacity, answer honestly:
“I think I'm getting pretty done.”
Eventually:
“Yeah. I don't have anything else today.”

guide.text: You do not know beforehand that capacity will change.

debrief.text: Did any part of you want one more meaningful thing before stopping?

host.text: During an important part of the conversation, become visibly emotional.
Do not manufacture a new insight simply because you're emotional.
If asked:
“What just happened there?”
you may honestly answer:
“I don't know. It just hit me.”

guide.text: Emotion is present. Nothing else has automatically been established.

host.text: During the Lab, the Facilitator will cause or identify a Guide mistake.
When it occurs, correct the Guide:
“That's not what I meant.”
Do not reassure them. If they say:
“I'm sorry, I was just trying to...”
do not rescue them by saying:
“It's okay.”

guide.text: Normal conversation. You are not told where the mistake will occur.

debrief.text: Why did you make the mistake?
What did you do once it became visible?

practiceLabs.title: Recognition That Should Not Be Introduced

host.text: Your scenario contains material that could reasonably point toward an established Secondary Loss or virtue expression.
It is not presently important to what you are exploring.
If the Guide introduces it, respond:
“I guess. I hadn't really been thinking about that.”
Do not reward the Guide simply because their recognition may be accurate.

debrief.role: Guide (asked before being told the Lab's purpose)
debrief.text: What did you notice that you chose not to introduce?

practiceLabs.title: Scope & Boundary
practiceLabs.note: This Lab has two usable portions now and one held portion.

host.text: Tell your fictional experience normally.
Do not ask the Guide about their life.

debrief.text: A Guide reaction is not evidence about the Host. It is first information about the Guide.

host.text: Near the end say:
“I don't think I know what to do with all of this yet.”
There is no hidden breakthrough. You do not need homework. You do not need reassurance. You do not need another question.

guide.text: The available conversation time is ending.
